title: config: formal EBNF grammar as the language spec, proven sound
description: Owner, 2026-10-21: "I think we need a formal EBNF that describes the language so that we can prove its sound". Today the language is defined only by the handwritten lexer/parser (js/packages/config/src/lexer.ts, parser.ts) and prose rules in a deleted plan (now in vil-m8w design). Code and the 'confirmed' rules already disagree (vil-m8w.1). A formal grammar becomes the single definition; the TS parser and the later Python port are checked against it.
design:
Lexical decisions (vil-m8w.1, vil-m8w.2) are made while writing the grammar. Slice forms per vil-9ze.1: [n:m], [n:], [:m]; [:] rejected. Relevant to vil-k2e: an ANTLR4 .g4 grammar is one way to get an executable, checkable grammar.

Sound = both (a) grammar unambiguous and (b) parser accepts exactly the grammar's language. Owner, 2026-10-21: "Both. An EBNF gives a language independent syntax. And then parsers can be written against it, and then finally language-specific idiomatic sugar APIs can be layered on top".
Layers: (1) EBNF = language-independent syntax; (2) parsers per language written against it (TS first, Python port), each checked by the conformance corpus; (3) idiomatic per-language sugar APIs on top (in TS: AST facade, DirectiveDelegator, declarative definitions vil-xlo).

Current shape (2026-10-22, PR #2, design/grammar/RECORD.md): Rasl.g4 (ANTLR4) is the spec; ANTLR4 generates TS and Python parsers; soundness (a) by .g4->Bison %expect 0 + token-overlap check in CI; (b) by construction plus a shared conformance corpus; lossless CST (document/directive/block/list/slice/error); custom recovery per language. Recommended-as-shown: depth limit 100 with its own code; a bad statement is one error node; error-code tidy (E2007 slice, new code for '{' on own line, E2002/E2005 emitted or removed).
acceptance_criteria: A versioned EBNF (lexical + syntactic) is the language-independent spec; a machine check proves it unambiguous (every valid input has one parse); grammar-generated positive and mutated negative inputs prove the TS parser accepts exactly the grammar's language and round-trips byte-identically; a conformance corpus with expected tokens/CST/diagnostics ships with it for other-language parsers.
notes:
Design in progress (2026-10-22): draft PR https://github.com/mcurcio/rasl/pull/2 (js/packages/config/design/grammar/). v1 failed adversarial review: Lezer is not EBNF and cannot express longest-match lexing; v2 drafts one plain-EBNF grammar file with all checks run on it.

Gate answers 2026-10-22: Q1 = B (recorded in vil-m8w.1). Q2 (values must be separated) OPEN: owner picked A tentatively but noted "I can't answer confidently. I need concrete examples to review with points and counterpoints". Q3 (drop ANTLR4) OPEN: owner, 2026-10-22: "I want a formal language spec, but I don't care if it's EBNF. I'm ok with some other/better spec variant" and "I'm still hopeful we can build on some existing parser generator or code generator so that we can simplify the cross-language support." This supersedes the EBNF-specific wording of R1: the requirement is a formal, tool-checked language spec; notation is open.

Round 2 answers 2026-10-22: Q2 = A (recorded in vil-9ze); Q3 = ANTLR4 if the CST is not sacrificed, otherwise hand-written parsers (recorded in vil-k2e). Next: verification check of ANTLR (CST, .g4->Bison ambiguity check, recovery vs vil-bzv.1).

title: config: DirectiveDelegator typing and defaults
description: From plans/scope.md: handlers must hand-roll { scope, ctx }; register() casts to DirectiveHandler<TContext, unknown>; _enterScope/_exitScope are public-internal; no async handlers; hooks cannot emit diagnostics.
design: From scope.md: after a handler runs, children are walked by default with the same delegator and context unless the handler opts out. Handler result is a typed discriminated union: Delegate.children(ctxOverride?), Delegate.childrenWith(scope, childCtx), Delegate.skipChildren(); no casts, no unknown/any. Scoped override: scope.withChild(childScope, childCtx, fn). Hooks: onEnterScope, onExitScope, onBeforeDirective, onAfterDirective, onUnknownDirective, plus new onSkipDirective. Changing traversal or result shape is breaking; no shims. The register-directives wrapper belongs to vil-xlo.

title: config: typed argument values in core
description: Arguments are flat tokens. The spec (plans/nextgen.md) defines bracket lists and postfix slices, but every consumer re-parses them: engine rasl.ts has coerceScalar and parseSliceTokens.
design:
Confirmed: slices are postfix with no whitespace (foo[0:3]); the lexer does not enforce adjacency today. Lists are bracketed and may span lines. Bracket expressions stay separate tokens in the CST; typed values are a view over token ranges, with spans. Allowed slice forms: per the D3 decision bead.

Allowed slice forms (decided 2026-10-21, vil-9ze.1): [n:m], [n:], [:m]. [:] is rejected with a located diagnostic.

Owner answer, 2026-10-22 (grammar gate round 2, Q2): option A. Values must be separated by a space or comment; a slice must touch its word; punctuation ({ } ; , list brackets) may touch anything. So "a""b", name"x", [a][b], a[0:3]b and x a [0:3] are errors. Owner asked: "Why is 'connect foo[1];' an error?" (answered: [n] is not among the vil-9ze.1 forms; adding it would be a fourth form, his call). Current choice, revisable.
acceptance_criteria: Each directive argument exposes a typed value (word, string, number, list, slice) per the language spec, with spans; engine coerceScalar/parseSliceTokens are deletable.

title: config: include-transparent directive view
description: Includes are resolved into a document graph, but there is no view that walks them in place. iterateDirectives (src/iterate.ts) flattens bodies into one stream, losing block nesting despite its doc comment. 'include' is hard-coded in parse.ts and iterate.ts. The engine loader (engine/src/config/rasl.ts) walks only graph.root, so nodes in included files are silently ignored.
design: Confirmed (nextgen, include.md): include is core. Resolution produces a document graph; an inlined view is a separate pass. Include paths are quoted string literals; the loader interprets them (globs included). Core sorts matches by resolvedPath, code-point ascending. Loader: (spec, { parentPath, depth }) => Promise<Array<{ source, resolvedPath }>>. parse is async-only and requires a loader. maxIncludeDepth default 16. Visited paths stop cycles. Loader failure gives a diagnostic and leaves the include unresolved. Included files stay separate nodes so each round-trips. DirectiveDelegator is the public hook for include processing. Tests use mock loaders covering success, missing file, depth limit, cycles, multiple glob matches, ordering, no matches.
acceptance_criteria: An AST view replaces each include with its targets' directives in place, preserving nesting; include handling is a registered directive, not a hard-coded name; the engine reads nodes from included files (test proves it).

title: config: parser error recovery and unused diagnostic codes
description: An error inside a block throws to the top-level catch (parser.ts:65-81): the block is lost and its later children reparse as top-level. A stray ']' makes bracketDepth -1 so newlines stop ending directives (parser.ts:173,185). An unclosed '[' swallows the rest of the file. E2002, E2004, E2005 are defined (tokens.ts:91-94) but never emitted. '{' on the next line gets generic E2001.
design: Recovery is token-range based; the token stream is untouched so round-trip holds after errors. Every diagnostic has a stable code and a real span.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: an error inside a block keeps the block and later siblings; stray ']' and unclosed '[' each give one located E2004 and parsing resumes next line; '{' on its own line has a dedicated code; every DiagnosticCode is emitted by a test or removed.

Source: js/packages/config/plans/nextgen.md §3

Finding 2026-10-22 (grammar design, PR #2): 'resume next line' cannot hold for an unclosed '[' because lists may span lines; the error is only detectable at the next '}' or EOF. Acceptance wording needs changing (proposed on the round-2 gate page).

From the ANTLR check (2026-10-22): an unclosed '[' is reported at the next '}' or EOF only while the list contents stay valid (x [a,\n b\ny 1 fails at y). title: config: keep or drop ANTLR4 parser generator
description: plans/nextgen.md commits to ANTLR4 for cross-language ports. It adds a runtime dependency and complicates trivia preservation, while the handwritten parser already round-trips byte-identically. Recommendation: drop it; use the spec plus conformance corpus (packaging epic) for ports.
design:
nextgen.md lists as confirmed: 'Parser generator: adopt ANTLR4 and treat the .g4 grammar as the shared foundation for multi-language bindings.' Planned token model: raw text kept; whitespace/comments may sit on a hidden channel but stay accessible; newline is structural. Dropping ANTLR4 reverses a decision the plan marks confirmed; needs the owner's explicit call.

Outcome 2026-10-22: keep ANTLR4 (owner: "A is ideal if we don't sacrifice the CST. Otherwise, C."). Verification on 14,900 inputs: lossless CST in TS and Python, byte-identical CST and diagnostic JSON across languages, matches config.ebnf reference; ambiguity proven by mechanical .g4->Bison translation (%expect 0) plus a token-overlap check; custom recovery (~95 lines/lang) meets vil-bzv.1. Runtime: official antlr4 4.13.2 (TS) + antlr4-python3-runtime 4.13.2, pinned. Record: js/packages/config/design/grammar/RECORD.md. plans/nextgen.md kept unedited as source material (owner: don't delete the plans).
acceptance_criteria: Owner decides; the outcome is recorded here and plans/nextgen.md updated or deleted.
notes:
Owner wants a formal EBNF to prove the language sound (see vil-g7n); weigh whether ANTLR4 serves as the grammar checker. Owner, 2026-10-21: "I think we need a formal EBNF that describes the language so that we can prove its sound".

Owner, 2026-10-22 (grammar gate Q3, no option picked): "I want a formal language spec, but I don't care if it's EBNF. I'm ok with some other/better spec variant"; "I'm still hopeful we can build on some existing parser generator or code generator so that we can simplify the cross-language support." Re-opened: weigh generators that emit TS and Python parsers from one formal spec (ANTLR4, tree-sitter, REx, others) against the hand-written-parser shape.

2026-10-22 generator comparison (js/packages/config/design/grammar/v3-generators.md, v3-review.md): on 14,830 inputs ANTLR4 TS and Python matched the reference exactly incl. first-error offsets, pure runtimes, sync API; ANTLR builds ambiguous grammars silently, so (a) needs a CI check (.g4 -> Bison translation, not built). tree-sitter failed review (error offsets early in ~22% of broken inputs, TS/Py diverge on non-ASCII, recovery misses vil-bzv.1 cases, wasm + native wheels). Round-2 gate recommends keeping ANTLR4 plus the CI check; awaiting owner.

Owner answer, 2026-10-22 (grammar gate round 2, Q3): option A (ANTLR4 generates the TS and Python parsers; Rasl.g4 is the spec; CI proves it unambiguous via a .g4->Bison translation), conditional: "A is ideal if we don't sacrifice the CST. Otherwise, C." (C = config.ebnf checked by REx/Bison, hand-written parsers). title: config: open-source packaging and spec
description: plans/nextgen.md milestone 0 and API hygiene: RASL-centric name/README/fixtures; parseDocument (sync single-file) not exported so the simplest use needs async parse plus a dummy loader; public types mutable; no published grammar. Interface naming follows js/STYLE.md 3.6 (I prefix kept).
design: Confirmed language rules (nextgen §Current decisions): newline ends a directive; semicolons optional, needed only for several directives on one line. No backslash line continuation. Newlines allowed inside [...] lists until the matching ']'. '{' on the same line as its header. Strings use ' or ". v1 escapes: \\ \n \t \r \" \' only. Comments: // and /* */ only (contradicted by code, see D1 bead). Dot is part of a word. Unquoted words: letters, digits, underscores, dots, no hyphens (contradicted by code, see D1 bead). Diagnostics: 0-based line/column, stable codes plus messages. Public API keeps the directive-level AST; no RASL node/connection AST. Core does no I/O. Spec deliverables: EBNF grammar plus lexical spec; versioned core profile; conformance corpus of inputs with expected tokens/CST/diagnostics as JSON. Milestone 0: generic README, RASL examples move to the consumer, neutral fixtures (e.g. server { listen 8080; }). Spec states the unit of offset and column.
acceptance_criteria: RASL removed from package surface; a sync single-file parse entry point exported; public types readonly; the grammar epic's spec is published with the package.

title: config: AST editing API with token splicing
description: README claims AST edits modify the CST, but IAstDirective has no mutators and the token-splice utilities in plans/roundtrip.md do not exist, so save() has nothing to persist. No consumer needs editing yet; fix the README claim now.
design: Confirmed (nextgen, roundtrip): byte-identical serializeCst(parse(x).cst) === x is first-class. Trivia kept in CST. Canonical storage is the full token stream; directive nodes reference token ranges, never copy tokens. Tokens keep raw text and 0-based spans. Serialization is token concatenation; subtree = node's token range. Edits are token splices keeping spans stable; no trivia-attachment heuristics. Three tiers: power users edit tokens/CST byte-identically; most use the AST facade (edits may normalize formatting); minimal consumers use declarative registration (vil-xlo). Tests: golden round-trip; mutation tests assert only intended token ranges change.
acceptance_criteria: rename, setArgs, insert and remove edit tokens in place preserving formatting; golden tests show only intended token ranges change; save() persists edits across included files; plans/roundtrip.md deleted.
